summary: Mark Simonson's launch page for Proxima Vara, the variable (wght, wdth, ital) version of Proxima Nova. Nearly everything is a tester: photographed props (a matchbox, VHS tapes) whose printed lettering morphs with sliders, an editable article whose headline, body and byline each get their own sliders, and three sticker-like editable lines. Every slider label is set in its own axis ('Weight' bold, 'Width' wide, 'Slant' slanted). A fixed green launch strip with a dark-mode switch and a red rotating-text 'Licensing & Purchasing Info' seal frame the page.

instances.look: Fixed ~25px neon-green (#00ff7c) strip across the top of every screen: 'Introducing Proxima Vara, a new variable font by Mark Simonson' in small condensed bold at the left, 'Switch to dark mode | Auto' links at the right (never cut as a block, attached to 00)

'Proxima' in Black upright and 'Vara' in Thin italic run together at ~238px in charcoal on white, then a red circular seal with 'LICENSING & PURCHASING INFO' set around its edge beside 'Proxima Nova goes variable! Change width, slant, and weight to get any style you can imagine. Try it today! ↓'
instances.feel: Cheerful, salesy in a good way
instances.ux: The seal links to the licensing page; 'Try it today! ↓' points at the testers below
instances.learn: Set the name's two words at opposite corners of the design space (Black roman vs Thin italic): the wordmark alone announces 'variable'
